subject: Discovery follow-up: pilot alignment, metrics & access requests
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@aquila-logistics.com>, Tom Hernandez <tom.h@aquila-logistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery follow-up: pilot alignment, metrics & access requests

Hi Samira / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the proposed pilot scope so we have a single source of truth before we lock dates: 

Pain points you described:
- High variance in inference latency across peak routing windows that breaks downstream SLA enforcement.
- Per-request cost spikes when billing spikes occur during load; existing caches are limited.
- Security: end-to-end auditability and data residency for PII-sensitive routes.

Pilot goals (30 days, internal-facing shipment triage use case):
1) Reduce 99th percentile Latency for the triage endpoint from ~1.6s to <=0.9s.
2) Demonstrate stable unit cost per 1k tokens with Redwoods' batching + caching — target 20% cost reduction vs current baseline.
3) Verify audit logs and VPC egress restrictions meet your compliance checklist.

Proposed scope & success criteria:
- Model variant: Open-Llama-13B quantized (we'll provision compatible variant if you prefer a different family).
- Workload: 10k requests/day ramping to 50k/day; typical sequence length ~220 tokens.
- Prompt/eval plan: we will run a 200 example prompt set (attached MVP_prompt_set_v1.csv) and the regression harness we discussed.
- Owners: Redwood engineering lead (Marissa) for runtime wiring; Aquila SRE (Samira) for network & auth; Product (Tom) to confirm functional acceptance.

Immediate access/setup asks (what we need from you):
- Short-lived service account in your dev VPC with outbound to our collector IP range (see network_access_checklist.pdf).
- Sample traffic export (anonymized) for one hour to understand sequence length distribution.
- Point of contact for procurement/PO (we'll need a signed order if you want Dedicated capacity after pilot).

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the metric targets above or propose adjustments (reply by EOD Monday 1/19).
2) Samira to share network allowlist and a dev-service-account by 1/21.
3) Marissa and I will schedule a 30-minute kickoff to confirm rollout plan and assign infra tasks (target: week of 1/26).

Attaching: MVP_prompt_set_v1.csv (prompt examples), network_access_checklist.pdf, pilot_timeline.xlsx.

If this captures everything, I'll turn this into a mutual action plan and send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Karthik
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[karthik.iyer@redwood.com]

[Attachment: MVP_prompt_set_v1.csv (CSV, 24KB)]
[Attachment: network_access_checklist.pdf (PDF, 12KB)]
[Attachment: pilot_timeline.xlsx (XLSX, 8KB)]

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@aquila-logistics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hernandez <tom.h@aquila-logistics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: pilot alignment, metrics & access requests

Thanks Karthik — this is a clear summary and lines up with our notes. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Security: we will need a short architecture diagram for the audit logs (what fields you capture and retention window). Can Marissa share that prior to the kickoff?
- Baseline metrics: our 99th currently averages ~1.52s (shipping triage endpoint). The cost baseline calculation — can you confirm whether it includes embedding calls? Our workflows call embeddings for metadata enrichment; if included, that will change the expected delta.
- Network: we can provide a dev service account. We'll need a contact in your infra team to validate the IP allowlist during the window.

If you can answer the above, we'll confirm the allowlist and try to provide the anonymized sample traffic by 1/21.

Samira
Senior SRE, Aquila Logistics
samira.k@aquila-logistics.com

> Hi Samira / Tom —
> 
> Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the proposed pilot scope so we have a single source of truth before we lock dates: 
> ...

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@aquila-logistics.com>, Tom Hernandez <tom.h@aquila-logistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Olivia Grant <olivia@consult-ops.io>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: pilot alignment, metrics & access requests

Appreciate the fast reply, Samira — answers inline below and next actions.

- Audit logs: yes — Marissa, attaching a one-pager that lists the fields we capture, retention defaults, and available export formats. Please confirm if you need a longer retention or field-level exclusions.
- Embeddings: thanks for the flag. The cost projection I referenced excluded embeddings for simplicity; for your workload we'll include an embedding+generation blended estimate. I'll update the cost delta in the MAP.
- IP allowlist validation: Marissa (cc'd) will be the infra lead to validate allowlist and coordinate a quick test during provisioning.

Updated asks and commitments:
1) Aquila: provide dev service account and anonymized 1-hour sample traffic by 1/21.
2) Redwood: updated MAP with blended cost estimates and a short audit-log one-pager (attached).
3) Kickoff: 30-min runbook + owner alignment — propose Wed 1/28 at 10:00 AM PT (Marissa to send invite).

I've also attached the MVP prompt set and a brief eval rubric so we can agree on pass/fail thresholds before running the regression.

If that works, Samira/Tom — please reply with any blockers; if not, propose alternate dates.

Thanks,
Karthik

[Attachment: audit_logs_onepager.pdf (PDF, 6KB)]
[Attachment: eval_rubric.md (MD, 4KB)]
